news.text: Most of the house is closed for renovation. The Entry, the Office, the Sundial Court, and the Archive are open, and the Archive's log book is the new catalogue.
The palace has a name: the Wending House. Also: gardens, a carriage clock, and the planets tracked.
The Entry gets a notice board, a link board, and an almanac.
The engraved view: rooms in three dimensions, lit by the real sun.
Lily Pads: sticky growth in a pond.

puzzles.q: A bat and a ball cost $1.10 together. The bat costs $1.00 more than the ball. What does the ball cost?
puzzles.a: Five cents. (Not ten: then the bat would cost $1.10 and the pair $1.20.)

puzzles.q: Remove two opposite corners from a chessboard. Can the remaining 62 squares be tiled by 31 dominoes?
puzzles.a: No. Opposite corners have the same color, so 32 squares of one color remain and 30 of the other, but each domino covers one of each.

puzzles.q: A hundred lockers stand closed. Student k toggles every k-th locker, for k = 1 to 100. Which lockers end up open?
puzzles.a: The perfect squares, 1, 4, 9, …, 100: ten lockers. A locker is toggled once per divisor, and only squares have an odd number of divisors.

puzzles.q: How many zeros does 100! end in?
puzzles.a: 24: there are 20 multiples of 5 up to 100, and 4 multiples of 25 contribute one more 5 each.

puzzles.q: What is the last digit of 7<sup>2026</sup>?
puzzles.a: 9. The last digits of powers of 7 cycle 7, 9, 3, 1, and 2026 leaves remainder 2 when divided by 4.

puzzles.q: In how many ways can a 2 × 10 strip be tiled by 1 × 2 dominoes?
puzzles.a: 89, a Fibonacci number: a tiling of a 2 × n strip ends either in one upright domino or in two flat ones, so the counts satisfy the Fibonacci recurrence.

puzzles.q: Which positive integers can be written as a sum of two or more consecutive positive integers?
puzzles.a: Exactly those that are not powers of 2.

puzzles.q: How many squares, of all sizes, are there on a chessboard?
Below 100, which pair of numbers makes Euclid's algorithm take the most steps?
puzzles.a: 89 and 55, consecutive Fibonacci numbers, which take 9 steps. (See Lamé's Corridor.)

puzzles.q: On the island of knights and knaves, A says: “We are both knaves.” What are A and B?
puzzles.a: A is a knave and B is a knight. A knight could never say it, so A lies, and the statement is false, so not both are knaves.

puzzles.q: On the same island, A says: “At least one of us is a knave.” What are A and B?
puzzles.a: A is a knight and B is a knave. If A were a knave, the statement would be true, which is impossible; so A tells the truth, and B must be the knave.

puzzles.q: Ten people meet, and each shakes hands once with each of the others. How many handshakes are there?
What is the sum of the first 100 odd numbers?
puzzles.a: 10,000. The first n odd numbers always sum to n², as an L-shaped layer added to a square.
